title: Orioles’ Colton Cowser calls game with dramatic home-run robbery at Coors Field
content:
Consider it another chapter in the Baltimore Orioles’ 2026 campaign, one that started with anticipation after the club landed Pete Alonso in free agency, drifted into disappointment, and, most recently, resulted in a light sell-off at the trade deadline.

Needing one win to reach .500 on the season, center fielder Colton Cowser called game in Baltimore’s 2-1 win over the Colorado Rockies on Monday. Using every inch of his 6-foot-3 frame, the 2021 first-round pick leaped at the wall of Coors Field to rob Jake McCarthy of what would have been a walk-off two-run home run.

Catch of his life?

“Situation and probably level of difficulty, yes,” Cowser told reporters postgame. “But I had one still, it was in Triple A in Norfolk on a 10-foot wall that I was able to rob. So, but that one was — this one was better, for sure.”

The Orioles, winners of eight of their last 10 contests, are 69-69 and surging in what has been an otherwise meager American League. Their recent stretch has put them just a half-game back of the Cleveland Guardians for the AL’s third and final wild-card spot.

Baltimore entered Monday with postseason odds at 21.5 percent, per FanGraphs, and with a remaining strength of schedule at .508, the second-hardest among teams competing for a postseason berth in the AL.

Two more games against the lowly Rockies, plus 10 straight against the Boston Red Sox (four games) Guardians (three) and Toronto Blue Jays (three) should give Baltimore enough headway to stake its claim for a postseason spot. The Orioles also have three games in mid-September against the New York Mets.

For the Rockies, the moment was simply more misery in a lost season. The club has now lost five straight, as well as 10 games at home dating back to the beginning of August against the Tampa Bay Rays. At 52-86, the Rockies have MLB’s worst record, and their minus-143 run differential is the worst in the National League and second-worst in MLB.
